_meta.purpose: One pack per country the pipeline may search. A pack is the whole country-specific decision: whether it is searched at all, which registered sources serve it, and what its default savings floor is together with where that figure came from.
_meta.self_contained_rule: A pack names only its own country. Nothing in one pack reads another, and enabling a pack must leave every other country's stored output byte-identical (T028). That is why sources are named per pack rather than inherited from a global default that shifts when a pack is added.
enablement_vs_resolution: Enabling a country decides what is SEARCHED. It does not decide what can be
READ: location resolution knows all 45 countries in country_preferences.json
either way, so a posting whose location resolves to a disabled country is
still resolved correctly and simply never fetched. Conflating the two would
make a posting's stored country depend on which packs happen to be on.
floors_are_unsourced_on_purpose: Every pack below ships default_savings_floor: null. Not one of these five
countries has a sourced monthly savings floor yet, and writing a plausible
number here would be exactly the fabrication the whole design refuses —
these figures decide whether an opportunity reaches a shortlist.
Resolution (T041) then does two different things, both correct: PK is on
countries_requiring_own_floor and reports 'UNSCORED — default not yet
sourced', while the others fall through to the global USD 2,000 fallback and
say 'fallback' as their floor_source, so nothing claims to be local data.
U1 in PLAN.md §11 is the task of sourcing the PK figure with its basis.

packs.name: Pakistan
packs.floor_note: Stays null. Applying the global USD 2,000 fallback to Pakistan produces a permanently empty shortlist, and inventing a replacement is a fabricated number. See U1.
packs.source_note: No Pakistan-specific board in the registry returned a usable feed on the 2026-08-08 probe. The corpus holds 10 PK postings out of 4,402, all from worldwide-remote sources. A PK-specific source is outstanding work (U2), and until one exists this pack says so rather than implying coverage it does not have.

packs.name: United States
packs.source_note: 13 of the 14 probed Greenhouse boards and 2 of 3 Lever boards are US-headquartered, which is why the corpus is 1,891 US postings out of 4,402. That is a property of the source list, not of the market.

packs.name: United Kingdom
packs.source_note: No GB-headquartered board is registered; GB postings arrive as UK offices of employers on the boards above. 263 in the corpus.

packs.name: Germany
packs.source_note: arbeitnow is Germany-weighted and is the only country-specific aggregator in the registry. 283 DE postings in the corpus. 148 of the 4,402 postings demand German, which eligibility compares against the user's own confirmed languages.

packs.name: Australia
packs.source_note: Thinnest of the five: 60 postings in the corpus, all Australian offices of employers on US-headquartered boards. An AU-specific source is outstanding (U2).

packs.name: Italy
packs.disabled_reason: Registered and off. Present so enabling a sixth country is a flag rather than a code change, and so T028 has a real pack to switch on when it asserts the other five stay byte-identical.

packs.name: Sweden
packs.disabled_reason: Registered and off, although one probed Lever board is Sweden-headquartered. Its postings arrive today only when another enabled pack names the same provider, which is a property worth seeing rather than hiding: a provider is shared, a pack is not.
